key_insight: Sparse AFM scans can be expanded into a probabilistic ensemble of plant cell-wall microstructures that maps to distributions of effective elastic properties rather than a single constitutive law.
engineering_relevance: This enables multiscale mechanics predictions for cotton fiber cell walls that preserve uncertainty from nanoscale imaging through macroscale tensile response.
method: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion with LoRA to generate AFM-like cell-wall microstructure ensembles from limited scans.
Evaluate synthetic microstructures using microfibril crossover count and crossover angle, then convert images to spatially varying modulus and Poisson's ratio fields.
Run strain-controlled finite element homogenization across an image ensemble and stiffness-ratio sweep, then propagate effective properties into stochastic tensile simulations.
evidence_signal: The study uses generated AFM-like images, homogenized property distributions, and 20 stochastic tensile realizations to show that effective modulus and Poisson's ratio vary strongly with matrix-to-fibril stiffness ratio and can appear multimodal.
watch_item: The intensity-to-property mapping is not yet calibrated against nanomechanical measurements, so the fiber-scale values are still qualitative rather than fully predictive.
paper_title: From Sparse AFM Observations to Probabilistic Macroscale Mechanics: A Generative-Physics Framework for Plant Cell Walls
